### 2026-10-10 – I did the firmware for the project. I was honestly a bit worried about the firmware, not sure if I could get it done properly, but the actual difficulty wasn't actually bad at all. I used RMK, and I d

**3h**

I did the firmware for the project. I was honestly a bit worried about the firmware, not sure if I could get it done properly, but the actual difficulty wasn't actually bad at all. I used RMK, and I didn't even have to touch the code itself, it was just a bunch of configuring stuff. I read through the RMK docs, and while it was quite a lot of reading, it was all pretty straigthforward to be honest. I configured the keyboard.toml with my wiring, layout, and keymap, and it mostly did the rest:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/e36f4ec9df6f514b24100fd5ec937bc068668dcff1c07dcd19d4dfcdcc406e62.png)

After that I had to make the vial.json file for reasons I do not fully understand, but for that I just needed to include my KLE  layout, and that was it. It ended up pretty ugly, so I won't include it, but it will be on the github.

After that was done most of the firmware was ready. One more thing I forgot to mention, is the design process of the layout. The base layer was pretty straigthforward, I tried making it feel as familiar as possible, while making it have all the keys I use frequently.

![my-keyboard](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/deda0b2c16a0eb411d578e2c4c93a83dc3c7e063f55cecd2f5ae4390020314d1.png)

The second layer was a bit more interesting, since I had a bit more of a choice over what went in. In the end, I ended up with this layout:

![my-keyboard1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/ccb957207804319d89119c0052a63f4a71693b933c96ddab445f57d0f65d36f4.png)
The top row has the numbers, for which I varied the order up a bit, with 0 being in front rather than at the end like in most keyboards. The reason I did it like this, since I normally use a hungarian layout keyboard,  which has the 0 in front(not sure why, but all hungarian keyboards have this), so I'm used to that, and it's always weird for me to use english keyboards because of this, so hope this will be better. It also has print screen for taking screenshots, pretty self explanitory.The second row is just the F keys, nothing really special about those. On the third row I have quite a lot of stuff, for example the Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste buttons are there so I can access my most used Control shortcuts with the Fn key too. I also have media controls, for which I usually use a macropad, but with this I can hopefully just use the keyboard. I also have the arrow keys in the corner, perfect place for them I think, since the keys are properly aligned there, and there's no layer shift, so it is natural to use them. I also have the backslash in place of Control, I just didnt have space for it on the base layer, so I put it her.

So that's it for today, and hopefully I can finish this tomorrow!

### 2026-10-11 – Built a CAD model for the keyboard. I mainly just exported the PCB from KiCad, so that was pretty straightforward. The only really more complicated part was doing the part of the design I'll print. I

**2h**

Built a CAD model for the keyboard. I mainly just exported the PCB from KiCad, so that was pretty straightforward. The only really more complicated part was doing the part of the design I'll print. I will use some M3x20 screws I have at home, and purchase some M3x10 screws for the feet. The main parts are the feet, and the cover for the pico. The feet are just to keep it suspended, so the pins don't touch my table, and it won't wobble. I also made a little cover for the pico, so it won't show, since the green would ruin the aesthetic. Here's the finished CAD model:

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 104643](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/f16ef5cba6b72b2d84466f60c6c12c67c9a160f21c51628fa7b066442a02e034.png)
